title: Fire coverage vs observed FDNY travel times (New York City)
question: How long does it take a fire unit to reach each part of the city, and does a drive-time model agree with what FDNY units actually achieved?

streets.about: NYC DoITT Citywide Street Centerline (CSCL), with posted_speed, trafdir, rw_type

zips.about: Modified ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (MODZCTA), with a list of member ZIPs

soql.$select: zipcode, count(*) as n, median(incident_travel_tm_seconds_qy) as med_travel_s, median(incident_response_seconds_qy) as med_response_s, avg(incident_travel_tm_seconds_qy) as avg_travel_s
soql.$where: valid_incident_rspns_time_indc='Y' AND incident_classification_group='Structural Fires' AND incident_datetime between '2025-01-01T00:00:00' and '2025-12-31T23:59:59'

observed.about: FDNY Fire Incident Dispatch Data, structural fires in 2025, medians by ZIP computed by the portal

assumptions: Units drive at the posted speed limit on the street centerline; no traffic, no siren speed-up.
The first unit comes from the nearest firehouse by drive time (FDNY may send another if that one is busy).
Where an incident happens inside a ZIP is unknown, so every street segment midpoint in the ZIP counts equally.

traps.check: The model estimates driving only. Observed incident_response_seconds_qy also includes turnout, so the comparison must use incident_travel_tm_seconds_qy.
FDNY marks records whose response time is not valid; only valid_incident_rspns_time_indc = 'Y' should be used.
Dispatch ZIPs are postal ZIPs, not polygons. They must be mapped to MODZCTA areas, and ZIPs that don't match (PO boxes, single buildings) reported, not dropped silently.
Medians from a handful of fires are noise; areas with fewer than min_incidents are excluded from scoring and listed.
